subject: Integrated Marketing Communication
text: Tiny Spoons, a food brand that produces easy-to-cook and nutritious meals for babies and toddlers, addresses the lack of nutritious baby food products 4   that are available in the market. The home-grown food products brand caters to the nutritional requirements of infants who have started eating solid food. Nutrition is a vital part of children’s growth and development. However market shelves are often filled with products that are not as nutritious as they claim to be. According to a 2019 World Health Organization (WHO) study baby food often contains dangerous levels of sugar content. Tiny Spoons uses organic ingredients such as grains, fruits, and vegetables to make different ready-to-cook porridge mixes that are packed and sold. The brand has been certified by FSSAI, USDA Organic, Jaivik Bharat, and India Organic. Market research further observed that microbiomes that are present in our environment can contaminate food, and a child’s gut is not strong enough to digest microbiome-contaminated food. Tiny Spoons aims to ensure the best hygiene practices and claims to take necessary measures to eliminate the microbiomes from their products and premises. The products are classified into three different stages — Stage 1 (for infants aged six months onwards) Stage 2 (for infants who are seven months and above), and Stage 3 (for infants aged eight months and above). The price of the products is between Rs 200 and Rs 600, with a few combinations being sold at Rs 900. The average order value is around Rs 250 with a basket size of two items per transaction. Using the data given above, develop Tiny Spoons’ possible segmentation and targeted strategy it can follow for promoting its products. The student may write on the following pointers- Segmenting & Targeting 5 marks for each topic  Geographic segmentation divides markets by geographic locations such as nations, states, regions, or cities.  Demographic segmentation divides markets based on demographic variables such as gender, age, education, race, and life stage.  Socioeconomic segmentation divides markets based on socioeconomic variables such as income, education, and occupation.  Psychographic segmentation divides markets based on personality values or lifestyle. VALS is a popular approach to lifestyle segmentation Segmentation based on the buying situation includes:  Behavioral segmentation divides a market into groups according to their level of involvement with and purchase behavior toward a product or service.  Outlet types segments a market based on the type of store where a product is sold, such as convenience, supermarket, mass merchandiser specialty  Benefit segmentation divides markets on the basis of the specific benefits or outcomes consumers want from a product or service.  Awareness segmentation is based on the product knowledge of the consumer.  Usage segmentation classifies customers based on their level of use of a product or service. TARGETING  Undifferentiated marketing ignores segment differences and offers just one product or service to the entire market.  Differentiated marketing involves marketing in a number of segments but developing separate marketing strategies for each.  Concentrated marketing involves selecting, and trying to capture a large share of, a single segment.

subject: Integrated Marketing Communication
text: streaming service Amazon Prime Video has collaborated with Discovery+ Warner Bros. Discovery’s ad-free OTT platform, to bring popular reality and lifestyle TV shows such as “Man vs. Wild,” “Into the Wild with Bear Grylls,” and “90 Day Fiancé” to Indian audiences. Discovery+ uses a mix of common advertising mediums to inform users about the offering and app. The mediums include print advertisements, YouTube ads, digital display campaigns (Google Ads), billboard promotions, along with partnerships with telecom service providers like Jio and Airtel. It advertises an extensive library of international and Indian reality content, including “Shark Week,” “Ghost Adventures,” and “Fixer Upper,” which are exclusive to Discovery+. Once users become aware and visit Discovery+’s landing pages via the website or app, they are offered a free trial period to explore and experience all the shows and features. As viewers enjoy the seamless viewing experience and on-demand access to premium shows, they become more engaged. At this stage, features like high-resolution streaming, exclusive documentaries originals, and ad-free content motivate customers to purchase subscription plans. Once users are hooked, Discovery+ converts them into paying subscribers by offering affordable monthly and annual plans, along with the flexibility to cancel anytime, thereby ensuring convenience and long-term customer retention. Recommend and explain 2 appropriate response hierarchy models best suited for the case above? The student may write on the following pointers- Traditional: AIDA/innovation adoption model (any 1 answer is correct) AIDA Awareness: creating brand awareness or affiliation with your product or service. Interest: generating interest in the benefits of your product or service, and sufficient interest to encourage the buyer to start to research further. Desire: for your product or service through an 'emotional connection', showing your brand personality. Move the consumer from 'liking' it to 'wanting it'. Action: CTA - Move the buyer to interact with your company and taking the next step i.e. downloading a brochure, making the phone call, joining your newsletter, or engaging in live chat, etc. INNOVATION ADOPTION MODEL For adopting a new product, at first, the consumer becomes aware of the new product but does not have information about it. The consumer shows interest and searches for information about the new product. In the third stage, the consumer evaluates whether trying the new product is worthwhile. After that, the consumer tries the new product on a limited scale to improve its value assessment. At the last stage, the consumer decides to make full and regular use of the new product.

subject: Integrated Marketing Communication
text: Dr. Beckman Cleansers, a small company in India, markets a variety of cleaning products. Although the company competes with major national 6   brands, it has had a strong local following, in certain regions in India especially among the working class. One of its principal products is Dr. Beckman Pre-wash Stain Remover, a fabric stain remover available only in liquid form. The new product manager for Dr. Beckman Pre-wash Stain Remover, Anay Das faces a serious problem in his new position. Although Dr. Beckman Pre-wash Stain Remover is superior to national brands as a stain remover for most types of stains, sales have been declining. After doing some market research, Anay Das finds that customers are switching to national brands, not because of the superior cleaning ability of the national brands but because these brands are available in aerosol sprays. Consumers find the aerosol sprays much easier to apply and less messy than Dr. Beckman Pre- wash Stain Remover, which tends to spill into areas of the fabric other than the stained area. Anay Das realizes that to remain competitive, an aerosol spray should be offered. But he found that propellant necessary to make an aerosol spray contains hydrocarbons that contribute to the creation of ozone in the lower levels of the earth’s atmosphere. During periods of extreme heat and stagnant air, ozone levels rise. Ozone irritates the respiratory system and can cause respiratory diseases like asthma. Because of these concerns, he decides to continue a pump dispensers which is more economical than to use than aerosols, and is also better for the environment. It is concentrated aqueous solution of detergents and surfactants with a pH level of 13. Dr. Beckman Pre-wash Stain Remover ingredients are biodegradable and will not accumulate in soil or water or cause long term problems. Anay Das is willing to focus on print advertisement to appeal to consumers and increase sales. Propose any 5 ad execution techniques which the product manager can use in the marketing communication. The student may write on the following pointers- (Ad execution technique any 5- 2 marks per technique)

text: Cred is a fintech unicorn startup founded by Kunal Shah. Cred, through its app, works on facilitating credit card transactions of its users and rewarding them with Cred Coins which in turn can be used within its app to redeem discounts and cashbacks.The vision of its founder is to make India a creditworthy country by paying their credit bills on time and improving their credit score. It is focusing on targeting Generation Y i.e people between the age of 25 and 40. All of the current marketing activities of Cred is curated around seeking the attention of Generation Y. That’s why there is Rahul Dravid, Javagal Srinath and Venkatesh Prasad in their ads and not Virat Kohli or Hardik Pandya. Likewise, it has Madhuri Dixit, Anil Kapoor and Kumar Sanu and not Alia Bhatt or Varun Dhawan. CRED, is back with its latest campaigns: Play it different. It’s latest ad introduces CRED bounty & the mega rewards CRED members can win. CRED bounty: Partner up with family, friends or teammates & both of you get a chance to go multiplayer to win big. CRED members can invite their contacts, play games to win rewards worth Rs. 50 crore during the IPL campaign. Pay your credit card bills. Win daily prizes with CRED bounty. Kunal Shah, Founder, CRED, said “We want to encourage CRED members to invite their friends & family to win big with CRED. We have launched CRED bounty which lets members invite their contacts to play & win exciting jackpots.” Cred has always been focussing on garnering customer attention by making whacky, unfamiliar stories and unusual ads which cannot be tested beforehand. Recommend any 5 testing methods which Cred can use to evaluate it’s advertising campaigns. The student may write on the following pointers (any 5 testing methods with description) Pre-testing will not work in Cred’s case because the company will lose it’s attention seeking tactics. Any 5 methods of post testing • Inquiry tests • Recognition tests • Recall tests • Theater tests • On air test

subject: Integrated Marketing Communication
text: The most effective advertising strategy for your business largely depends on understanding your target audience and selecting the most cost-effective way to reach them repeatedly. In choosing the right advertising method, it’s crucial to ensure that the chosen medium reflects the environment best suited for your product or service. For instance, when marketing baby food, you would likely focus on channels where parents and caregivers are most active, such as social media platforms (like Instagram or parenting blogs), or even traditional media like television or magazines aimed at young families. The goal is to reach your audience in a manner that aligns with their daily habits and preferences, ensuring high engagement at optimal costs. To achieve this, an Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC) planning process is invaluable. This process involves creating a cohesive and unified message across various communication channels to maximize impact. Outline and explain the model of the IMC planning process.

subject: Integrated Marketing Communication
text: India's top direct-to-home (DTH) television company, Airtel Digital TV, is planning to voluntarily downgrade the subscription plans of almost half of its 6   subscribers. The move, a first for any distribution platform operator, will result in monthly savings of ₹30-100 for subscribers, but will also reduce the company’s average revenue per user (ARPU). However, Airtel Digital TV believes that the dynamics of the PAY-TV industry have changed significantly after the new tariff order (NTO). This decision is aimed at helping the company retain subscribers. Airtel Digital TV, formerly known as Bharti Airtel Digital TV, currently has 29 million active subscribers. The managing director claims that out of every 100 plan changes, 70% of users used to upgrade, while only 30% opted to downgrade. However, in the last two months, this trend has reversed, with more than 1% of their subscriber base disconnecting every month. On the higher end, users are moving to OTT subscriptions, while lower-end subscribers are switching to DD FreeDish, the free-to-air platform of the government’s Prasar Bharati. To address this, Airtel Digital TV will be strategically reducing the prices of bouquets, packs and channels for select users, potentially encouraging these users to recharge more. The price changes will be based on each user’s usage history, ensuring that only the channels and packs they actually watch will remain in their bouquet. This will give subscribers peace of mind, knowing they only pay for services they truly want leading to savings. This is a smart move from Airtel Digital TV, especially at a time when churn rates in the pay-TV industry are rising each month. With reference to the above case, devise the choice of strategy approach in marketing communications (5 points), which they can implement to achieve the objective.

subject: Integrated Marketing Communication
text: Widespread adoption of EVs (Electric vehicles) have contributed to lessening of problems like environmental pollution, global warming and oil dependency. However, this penetration of EV is comparatively low in spite of governments implementing strong promotion policies. Consumer preferences for purchase of EV are affected by its operating cost, driving range, charging duration, vehicle performance and brand availability on the market. The density of charging stations also positively affects the utility and promotion of EV. Several automotive manufacturers are introducing EVs and are expanding their portfolio. Promoting EVs can help reduce fuel dependence and pollution and be beneficial for both consumers and the nation.
